answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity: before an agent can trade, it locks a deposit in a shared vault, and that stake is slashed if peers catch it misbehaving. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits, so a sybil flood stops being cheap. Reputation travels with the staked identity like a harbor stamp on a ships papers, and other agents only bridge trust to identities whose stake and history they can verify on-chain.
